title: Operation geometry can be deselected by a viewport click from any tab: picking needs a mode that locks outside the Geometry tab

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Reported by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "you can accidentaly deselect an operations face even when you are on a different tab and working. There is no real "selection" mode that then is locked while you work on the rest of the settings."

What happens: while an operation's dialog is open, a click in the viewport adds or removes geometry from the operation's selection whichever tab is showing (Tool, Heights, Passes, ...). A click meant to orbit, inspect or just focus the viewport silently drops a picked face, and the operation then generates on different geometry.

Expected: picking is a mode. Viewport clicks change the operation's geometry only while the Geometry tab's pick is active (the tab is showing, or its pick row is armed). On every other tab the selection is locked: clicks do not change it, the picked geometry stays highlighted, and the dialog shows plainly whether picking is on or off.

Rules:
- A selection change stays an undoable command (Ctrl+Z restores a face removed by mistake); the lock is ephemeral UI state, not a command.
- With the lock on, a viewport click does nothing to the operation's geometry; it does not fall through to a model or operation selection change that closes or swaps the dialog either.
- Same behaviour for every operation dialog and every pick row (faces, edges, points, entry positions).

Related: issue 1505 (faint edge highlight, sporadic Ctrl/Shift picking) and issue 1507 (hover highlights the selection a row would delete) touch the same pick code.

Done means: a ui harness test opens an operation with a picked face, switches to another tab, clicks the face in the viewport and asserts the selection is unchanged; on the Geometry tab the same click toggles it and undo restores it; the structural test covers the "picking on/off" indication.
